Consult Summary:
- 50-year-old female with 5–6 days of continuous dry cough and rhinorrhea; working impression: viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis (most likely).

History:
- Presenting complaint and timeline:
  - Dry, continuous cough for ~5–6 days, worse at night and disrupting sleep.
  - Concurrent rhinorrhea from onset.
  - Cough-induced throat irritation; no purulent sputum.
  - Subjective chills/feeling feverish (no temperature measured).
  - Generalized myalgias, marked fatigue and malaise.
  - Brief diarrhea at onset that resolved within a short time.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No chest pain.
  - No baseline shortness of breath; transient breathlessness only with coughing episodes.
  - No ear pain or discharge.
  - Appetite essentially preserved.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting or ongoing GI symptoms.
  - No hemoptysis, no focal chest pain, no reported anosmia/ageusia.
- Past medical history, allergies, medications:
  - Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - Hypertension.
  - Medications: metformin, lisinopril.
  - No known medication allergies.
- Social / preventive factors:
  - Lives with partner who is currently well.
  - Former smoker; quit ~6 months ago.
  - Alcohol: wine ~2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.
  - Occupation: software developer (sedentary job); has taken 1 day off work.

Examination:
- Vitals: none recorded in transcript.
- Clinician-observed findings:
  - Clinician noted a dry cough; no productive mucoid sputum heard/reported.
  - No documented focused physical examination (no chest auscultation findings recorded).
- No labs or imaging performed.

Impression:
- Working clinical impression:
  - Most likely: Viral upper respiratory infection / acute bronchitis.
    - Rationale: Acute 5–6 day history of rhinorrhea, dry nocturnal cough, myalgias, subjective fever/chills and transient diarrhea consistent with viral prodrome (clinician also stated likely viral).
  - Other considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
    - Influenza — possible given systemic symptoms (chills, prominent myalgias, marked fatigue); no measured fever recorded.
    - COVID-19 — presentation (dry cough, myalgias, subjective fever, transient diarrhea) is compatible; testing not performed.
  - Alternative / less likely:
    - ACE inhibitor–induced cough (lisinopril) — plausible because medication can cause dry nocturnal cough, but timing with acute viral symptoms and systemic features makes an infectious cause more likely.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none that change primary assessment; DDx highlights ACE inhibitor cough and COVID/influenza as considerations which are consistent as alternate possibilities.

Plan:
- Symptomatic/supportive care (as discussed by clinician):
  - Rest and reduce activity; stay well hydrated.
  - Regular paracetamol (acetaminophen) for symptomatic relief of fever/aches as needed.
  - Short period off work recommended (1–2 days) if possible; return when symptoms improve.
- Safety-net / follow-up instructions:
  - Return earlier if breathing worsens, chest pain develops, or clinical condition declines.
  - If not improving in 2–3 days, re-evaluation recommended; clinician suggested antibiotics may be considered if persistent fever and cough suggest bacterial chest infection.
- Additional recommendations consistent with DDx:
  - Consider testing for COVID-19 and/or influenza according to local public health guidance if symptoms persist or for infection control purposes.
  - If cough persists beyond expected post-viral period or no infectious cause identified, consider evaluating for ACE inhibitor–related cough and discuss substituting lisinopril with clinician/primary care provider.
- Investigations/referrals:
  - None performed today. Consider pulse oximetry, temperature measurement, or chest exam/auscultation and targeted testing if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation).
  - Focused physical exam findings (chest auscultation, lung fields).
  - COVID-19/influenza testing status and results.
  - Duration of lisinopril therapy (relevant to ACE inhibitor cough consideration).
  - Exact follow-up timing (specific date/time) and plan for who to contact for worsening symptoms.
  - Immunization history (influenza/COVID vaccines) and smoking pack-year history.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - Minor: DDx lists ACE inhibitor cough as a medium-likelihood cause; transcript clinician prioritized viral infection as primary diagnosis. (Conflict noted but does not alter immediate management.)
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear and coherent; patient history well obtained.
  - Lacks objective measurements and documented physical exam findings, limiting completeness of assessment.
